stem:
Ojas compares spinach grown on a nearby field with the same kind of spinach brought by truck from far away. Food miles are the travel from producer to consumer.

Why can choosing the nearby spinach help?

options.text: Shorter producer-to-consumer travel means fewer food miles, which can cut transport cost and pollution.
Spinach grown nearby always has fewer food miles, even if it travels through a distant warehouse first.
Putting the far-away spinach on sale reduces its food miles even when the truck route stays unchanged.
The greener-looking bunch has fewer food miles, even if it travelled farther.

teacher.key_rationale: Food miles measure producer-to-consumer travel. Nearby spinach with a shorter route has fewer food miles, which can lower transport cost and pollution. A distant warehouse, a sale price, or greener looks do not by themselves cut food miles.
